conventions.commits: Conventional Commits format with types (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore); all commits must be GPG-signed and signed-off with DCO
conventions.testing: Unit tests in module files (mod.rs, language/*.rs) using #[test] and #[cfg(test)]; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/ with SemanticExtractor for def-use analysis
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings (enforced: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used all deny)
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for error types, Option/Result patterns with .and_then() and .map(), bounds checking on byte slices before indexing

patterns: Language modules export ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as &str constants
Handler functions (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance) take &Node and &str (source) parameters
extract_inheritance returns Vec<String> with format strings like 'extends ClassName' or 'implements InterfaceName'
DEFUSE_QUERY captures write sites (local declarations, assignments) and read sites (identifier usage) with capture names like @write.local, @write.assign, @read.usage
Language registration in get_language_info() match statement with LanguageInfo struct populated with language name, tree-sitter Language, queries, and optional handlers
Extension map in lang.rs maps file extensions to language identifiers; supported_languages() array lists all language names
constraints: All languages unconditionally compiled in (no lang-* feature gates)
tree-sitter 0.27.1 API used; LANGUAGE constant from crate must be converted to Language via .into()
Query strings must be valid tree-sitter query syntax; capture names must match handler expectations
DEFUSE_QUERY is optional but recommended for languages with local variable scoping
Handlers must return Option or Vec; must handle byte bounds checking to avoid panics
test_coverage: Each language module includes unit tests for ELEMENT_QUERY (verifying class/function/interface extraction), inheritance extraction, and DEFUSE_QUERY (write/read site detection). Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/ verify end-to-end analysis with SemanticExtractor.extract_def_use_for_file(). Tests use stack-based tree traversal to find nodes and validate query results.

library_findings.notes: Crate provides PHP language support; grammar covers function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration nodes with base_clause and class_interface_clause for inheritance

library_findings.relevant_api: Language type, Node.child_by_field_name(), Node.kind(), Query, QueryCursor
library_findings.notes: Core parsing library; field-based node access used throughout language handlers

approaches.name: Minimal PHP support (CSS-like pattern)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY only; no handlers, no DEFUSE_QUERY. Register in mod.rs match arm and lang.rs extension map. Suitable if def-use analysis not required.

approaches.name: Full PHP support with handlers and DEFUSE_QUERY
approaches.description: Add php.rs with all queries (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY) and handlers (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance). Register in mod.rs and lang.rs. Comprehensive analysis matching Java/Kotlin pattern.
pros: Supports def-use analysis for local variables
cons: Requires thorough testing of all handlers

approaches.name: Phased approach: minimal first, handlers later
approaches.description: Phase 1: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY only (no handlers, no DEFUSE_QUERY). Phase 2 (follow-up PR): Add DEFUSE_QUERY and handlers. Allows incremental review and testing.
pros: Easier to test and validate incrementally
cons: Requires two PRs instead of one

recommendation: Approach 2 (Full PHP support with handlers and DEFUSE_QUERY). The issue title explicitly requests 'add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php' and the reference to 'model after java.rs' indicates full feature parity is expected. The codebase already has mature patterns for complete language support (Java, Kotlin, Go, C++, C#). A complete implementation in one PR is cleaner than phased approach and matches maintainer expectations. The medium complexity is justified by the comprehensive feature set.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}

inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-php grammar (common/define-grammar.js): class_declaration node has optional base_clause child (for extends) and optional class_interface_clause child (for implements). The base_clause contains a named_type node representing the superclass name. The class_interface_clause contains one or more named_type children, each representing an implemented interface. Extract by walking class_declaration children to find base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes, then extract text from their named_type children using node.start_byte()..node.end_byte() indexing into source.
